question: In May 2024, India signed a long-term agreement for the operation of Chabahar Port. What is the duration of this agreement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India signed a long-term agreement with Iran for the operationalization of the **Chabahar Port** in May 2024.
 
• The duration of the agreement is **10 years**, ensuring India's strategic and economic interests in the region.
 
• The Chabahar Port is India's gateway to **Afghanistan and Central Asia**, bypassing Pakistan.
 
• This port plays a critical role in the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**, enhancing regional connectivity.
 
• The agreement reflects India's commitment to strengthening its ties with Iran despite geopolitical challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chabahar Port**

 
 
• Located in southeastern Iran, Chabahar is the only Iranian port with direct access to the Indian Ocean.
 
• It consists of two terminals: **Shahid Beheshti** and Shahid Kalantari.
 
• The port is strategically important for India to bypass Pakistan for trade with Afghanistan and Central Asia.
 
 
 
• **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**
 
 
• An international multimodal transportation project connecting India, Iran, and Russia.
 
• It aims to reduce the time and cost of freight transport compared to the Suez Canal route.
 
• Chabahar Port is a key node in this corridor.
 
 
 
• **India-Iran Relations**
 
 
• India and Iran share strong cultural, economic, and strategic ties.
 
• Chabahar Port is a cornerstone of these bilateral relations.
 
• Both countries cooperate on counterterrorism and regional stability initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Significance**
 
 
• Chabahar Port counters China's influence in the region, particularly the Gwadar Port in Pakistan under the CPEC.
 
• It enhances India's connectivity with resource-rich Central Asia.
 
• The port is vital for the economic development of landlocked Afghanistan.
